title: Loupe: Driving the Development of OS Compatibility Layers
problem: Developers lack efficient methods to precisely measure which OS features are required by applications when building compatibility layers for new operating systems, resulting in large engineering inefficiencies and wasted development effort.
motivation: New operating systems must support mainstream applications to achieve real-world adoption and have meaningful impact.
method: Loupe provides a measurement tool and methodology to systematically identify and quantify OS feature requirements from applications. The approach analyzes application syscall and OS API usage patterns to determine which compatibility features must be implemented. This enables developers to prioritize implementation efforts based on actual application needs rather than guessing.
key_novelty: A practical measurement methodology that precisely quantifies which OS features are actually required by applications, enabling targeted and efficient development of OS compatibility layers.
contributions: Loupe tool for automated measurement of OS feature requirements from applications
Methodology for prioritizing OS compatibility layer implementation based on application demands
Empirical analysis of OS feature usage patterns across mainstream applications
Framework to reduce engineering inefficiency in building new OS compatibility layers

metrics.other: Feature coverage percentage, implementation effort reduction, application compatibility rate

primary_theme: OS feature measurement for compatibility layers
